successCriteria.description: PgEmployeeRepository implements IEmployeeRepository and maps every camelCase Employee field to its snake_case column (employee_number, first_name, last_name, manager_id, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) with no snake_case leaking into TypeScript field names and no camelCase in SQL.
EmployeeService implements IEmployeeService (create/update/terminate/reactivate) and delegates all persistence to IEmployeeRepository without importing the pool or a DB client.

PgLeavePolicyRepository implements ILeavePolicyRepository and maps LeavePolicy fields to snake_case columns (policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active).
PolicyService implements IPolicyService (create/update/activate/deactivate/findByLeaveType) and delegates persistence to ILeavePolicyRepository.

PgAuditLogRepository implements IAuditLogRepository, persists to the audit_logs table, and maps fields to snake_case columns (entity_type, entity_id, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at).
AuditService implements IAuditService (record/findByEntity/findByPerformedAt) and delegates persistence to IAuditLogRepository.
Each module's index.ts barrel re-exports its new repository and service implementations, and `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) passes with no type errors.

constraints: All SQL and DB access lives ONLY in the repository layer (GP-001); services never import the pool, a client, or a module-level DB helper.
The repository is the ONLY layer that maps camelCase TypeScript fields to snake_case DB columns; no snake_case in TS field names, no camelCase in SQL.

Services receive IUnitOfWork via constructor injection and own the unit of work; participating repository/service methods take the client as an optional LAST parameter and fall back to the shared pool when omitted. withTransaction is never placed on a repository.
No `any`; use `unknown` with type guards (HARNESS no-any rule).
Do not build routes, controllers, or tests in this phase; do not reference route files.
Modules import from each other only through their index.ts barrel; no cross-module internal imports.
outOfScope: Routes, controllers, and HTTP wiring for employee/policy/audit (deferred to Phase 2 part 3/3).
Jest unit/integration tests for these modules (deferred to Phase 2 part 3/3).
Knex migrations / DDL for the employees, leave_policies, and audit_logs tables.
RBAC enforcement and auth middleware (route-level concern, not applicable to layer-2 services).
The leave, balance, and notification modules.

ambiguities.description: Whether the audit module's record() should itself open a transaction (via IUnitOfWork) or be a single-step write that participates in a caller's transaction via the optional client parameter.
options: record() is a single-step write using the shared pool by default and joins a caller's transaction via the optional client
record() always wraps itself in withTransaction

ambiguities.description: Whether employee/policy service mutations (create/update/terminate/activate) must write an AuditLog record now, or whether audit recording is only wired when the leave orchestration module composes them.
options: Layer-2 services write audit records for their own state changes (GP-002 applies immediately)
Audit recording is deferred to the leave orchestration phase; these leaf services only persist their own entity

entityInvariants.invariant: employmentStatus is restricted to 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' | 'TERMINATED'; terminate() sets status to TERMINATED with a terminationDate, reactivate() restores ACTIVE and clears terminationDate; deletedAt is null for live rows and set on soft-delete.
isActive is a boolean lifecycle flag; activate()/deactivate() toggle it; entitlementDays is a non-negative integer; leaveType is a valid LeaveType enum value.
AuditLog is append-only (no update/delete lifecycle); every record carries a valid EntityType, AuditAction, and performedAt timestamp; oldValues/newValues are JSON-serializable objects or null.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IEmployeeRepository.create / findById / findByEmployeeNumber / findByEmail / update / delete
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: find* return null (not throw) when no row matches; update returns null when the id does not exist; delete returns boolean success.
terminate/reactivate on a non-existent employee return null; invalid employmentStatus transitions are rejected with a typed error rather than silently coerced.
find* return null when no row matches; findActiveByLeaveType filters isActive=true; update returns null when the id does not exist.
activate/deactivate on a non-existent policy return null; create with an invalid LeaveType is rejected with a typed error.
findById returns null when absent; findByEntity/findByPerformedAt/query return arrays (possibly empty), never null.
record persists and returns the created AuditLog; read operations return arrays (possibly empty).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Repository and service implementations must match the exact field names, types, and method signatures already declared in the layer-1 model/interface files (Employee, IEmployeeRepository, IEmployeeService).
EmployeeService must implement the exact IEmployeeService surface (create/update/terminate/reactivate) and CreateEmployeeInput shape.
Repository and service implementations must match LeavePolicy and ILeavePolicyRepository field names/types/signatures.
PolicyService must implement the exact IPolicyService surface and CreateLeavePolicyInput shape.
Repository and service implementations must match AuditLog, IAuditLogRepository, and AuditLogQuery field names/types/signatures.
AuditService must implement the exact IAuditService surface and AuditRecordInput shape.
Services must use the injected IUnitOfWork.withTransaction(fn) contract and never import the pool; participating methods take the client as an optional last parameter.
Repositories obtain DB access from the shared pool exported by connection.ts (fallback when no client is passed).
LeaveType, EntityType, and AuditAction must be imported from the shared types barrel, not redefined locally.

integrationPoints.why: Repositories execute SQL against the shared pg Pool as the default client when none is passed.
Services receive IUnitOfWork via constructor to own transaction boundaries for multi-step writes.
Policy and audit modules depend on shared enums for typed fields.
Barrels must re-export the new repository + service implementations for downstream consumers.
